divers.name: Ярина Затонська
divers.bio: Пірнаю з 2016 року. Люблю затонулі кораблі Червоного моря й печери Мальти. Інструкторка з Києва.

dives.notes: Арка на 55 м — не для нас, лишились над нею.
Дві довгокрилі акули на південному плато.

reviews.text: Найкращий затонулий корабель, який я бачила. Плануйте два занурення: одне ззовні, друге всередині трюмів.
Красиво, але людно з 10 до 14. Приходьте рано. Не заходьте глибше за свою кваліфікацію.
Вікно в синяву неймовірне. Вхід слизький, беріть черевики з твердою підошвою.
Видимість залежить від вітру. Цікаво для тренувань із компасом.

warnings.text: Арка лежить на 55 м: це нижче межі рекреаційного дайвінгу. Тут щороку гинуть дайвери. Не заходьте в неї без технічної підготовки.

posts.title: Тиждень на Thistlegorm
posts.text:
Шість занурень на одному кораблі, і щоразу щось нове. На першому оглянули корпус і локомотив на дні. На другому зайшли в трюм №2 з мотоциклами BSA. Нітрокс дуже допоміг: на 30 м часу стало вдвічі більше.

Порада: беріть ліхтар навіть удень, у трюмах темно.

posts.title: Дахаб для новачків
posts.text: Дахаб — найпростіше місце, щоб почати. Заходите з берега, течії майже немає, риф одразу біля входу. Lighthouse Reef — ідеальний для першого нічного занурення.

posts.title: Мальта взимку
posts.text: Вода 15 °C, туристів немає, а видимість 30 м. Сухий костюм — і всі печери Гозо ваші.

posts.title: Як я готуюся до глибоких занурень
posts.text: Чекліст перед зануренням нижче 30 м: план газу, нітрокс і його межі, резервний ліхтар, SMB, перевірка напарника. Нічого нового, але саме на цьому економлять.

posts.title: Одеса: затоплені баржі
posts.text: Наше море не тропіки, але затоплені баржі під Одесою — чудовий полігон для навігації та сухих костюмів.

posts.title: Чернетка: Ельфінстон
posts.text: Південне плато, дві акули…

posts.title: Елфінстоун на світанку
posts.text:
Вийшли з Марса-Алам о п’ятій ранку, щоб бути на рифі першими. Течія з півночі, тож пірнали від північного плато вздовж східної стіни.

На 25 м біля плато кружляли дві білопері акули. Час на дні короткий, тому все планування — на поверхні.

posts.title: Печера Елефант на Криті
posts.text:
Сталактити під водою — це не казка. Вхід на 10 м, далі темний коридор, де без котушки робити нічого.

Усередині знайшли кістки карликового слона. Гід каже, їм десятки тисяч років.

posts.title: Каньйон у Дахабі: вузько, але красиво
posts.text:
Зайшли в Каньйон з берега, спустились у щілину на 30 м. Світло падає згори смугами, як у соборі.

Порада: тримайте плавність, бо мул піднімається миттєво і видимість зникає.

posts.title: Блакитний грот на Бішеві
posts.text:
Найкраще світло опівдні, коли сонце заходить у грот під водою. Сам грот мілкий, але стіни навколо йдуть до 40 м.

Людей багато, тож пірнайте зранку або восени.

submissions.name: Odesa Lighthouse Breakwater
submissions.description: A breakwater by the Vorontsov lighthouse. Boulders, mussel beds and gobies. Visibility depends on the wind, best after calm days in late summer.

divers.name: Marco Rossi
divers.bio: Wreck diver from Cagliari. Nitrox and deco, mostly in the Mediterranean.

dives.notes: Barracuda school at the top of the pinnacle.
Toilets on the reef, as promised.
Oceanic whitetip on the safety stop.

reviews.text: The best wreck in the Adriatic. Cold and dark at the bottom, bring a proper torch and plan your gas.
Pinnacle dive with serious current. Big schools of barracuda and amberjack. Only with a good guide.
Easy to navigate, intact bridge. Can be busy at weekends.
Protected for decades and you can tell: huge groupers that are not afraid of divers.

warnings.text: Since the spring storms the mooring buoy is gone. Boats now drop divers in open water: use an SMB and agree on a pick-up plan.

posts.title: Baron Gautsch on nitrox
posts.text: Forty metres, fourteen degrees and twelve metres of visibility. The Baron is not an easy wreck, but it is the most rewarding one in the Adriatic. We dived it twice with EAN28 and decompressed on EAN50.

posts.title: Sardinia in October
posts.text: Water still at 22 degrees, no crowds and the barracuda are back on Secca del Papa. October is the best month here.

posts.title: Um El Faroud, a wreck with a story
posts.text:
The tanker sits upright at 36 metres off Wied iż-Żurrieq. The bridge is at 15 metres, so even a short dive shows a lot.

Penetration is easy through the engine room, but bring a torch and watch the silt.

posts.title: Medes Islands: groupers everywhere
posts.text:
Twenty years of protection show. Groupers the size of a scooter swim right up to the mask.

The Dolphin tunnel is the highlight, about 15 metres long and wide enough for two divers.

posts.title: Grotta dei Gamberi in winter
posts.text:
Sicily in February: 15 degrees in the water and nobody else on the boat. The cave entrance sits at 20 metres.

Inside, the ceiling is covered with red shrimp. Use a soft light so you do not scare them off.

posts.title: Why I plan deco on paper first
posts.text:
My computer is good, but I still write the plan on a slate before every deep dive. If the computer dies, the slate does not.

Two gases, two schedules, one backup table. Ten minutes on the boat saves a lot of stress at 40 metres.

submissions.name: Nereo Cave
submissions.description: The largest underwater cave in the Mediterranean, at Capo Caccia. Several entrances, red coral on the ceilings. A torch is a must; stay within daylight unless you are cave-trained.

divers.name: Aiko Tanaka
divers.bio: Divemaster travelling Southeast Asia. Macro photography and mantas.

dives.notes: Reef hook for 20 minutes, grey reef sharks.

reviews.text: World-class drift. You need a reef hook and you need to listen to the briefing: the current can switch.
Macro paradise. Slow down and look into every crack.
Permits are limited, book early. Turtles, sharks and the barracuda school on almost every dive.
Shore entry over black pebbles, easy for beginners. Go at sunrise before the day boats arrive.

posts.title: Twelve sites, five countries
posts.text: Two years of diving across Southeast Asia, in one post. Indonesia for variety, Palau for sharks, the Philippines for threshers, Malaysia for the barracuda and the Similans for macro. Where would I go back first? Raja Ampat, without a doubt.

posts.title: Liberty at night
posts.text:
The USAT Liberty is busy by day and magical by night. Parrotfish sleep in their mucus bubbles along the hull.

We saw a Spanish dancer on the stern. Bring a red light and move slowly.

posts.title: Mola season at Crystal Bay
posts.text:
August to October is the time. We waited at 30 metres on the cleaning station for twenty minutes, and then she came.

The water was 19 degrees with a thermocline. Bring a thicker suit than you think.

posts.title: Thresher sharks at Monad Shoal
posts.text:
Up at four, in the water at five. The threshers come to the cleaning stations at dawn.

Kneel on the rope line, no lights and no chasing. We saw six that morning.

posts.title: Richelieu Rock macro list
posts.text:
Seahorses, ghost pipefish, harlequin shrimp and a frogfish the size of a coin. The rock is small, so one tank covers it all.

If you are lucky, a whale shark passes by. We were not, but the macro was enough.

locker: Sony A7 IV in Nauticam housing

divers.name: Богдан Лиманець
divers.bio: Пірнаю в Україні з клубом «Дельфін». Чорне море, кар’єри й трохи Червоного моря.

reviews.text: Для тренувань ідеально: близько, неглибоко, є де зупинитися. Видимість — 2–3 метри.
Найцікавіше, що є в Чорному морі біля Одеси. Обов’язково з компасом.
Каньйон на 40 м, червоні горгонарії і бірюзова вода. Течія біля виходу.

warnings.text: На західній баржі обірвані рибальські сітки на 18–20 м. Майте ніж або різак для ліній.

posts.title: Чорне море: з чого почати
posts.text: У нас холодніше й темніше, ніж у тропіках, але навчитися тут — означає потім пірнати будь-де. Кілька порад про костюми, ліхтарі й навігацію.

posts.title: Зимове тренування на Київському морі
posts.text:
У лютому вода +3, видимість п’ять метрів. Тренувались з сухими костюмами й запасним регулятором.

Після занурення гарячий чай у машині — обов’язково.

posts.title: Затонулі баржі в Одеській затоці
posts.text:
Дві баржі на 18 м, обросли мідіями повністю. Видимість улітку до восьми метрів, якщо немає вітру з півдня.

Беріть котушку і буй: тут ходять катери.

posts.title: Каньйон у Каші для новачків
posts.text:
Каш у Туреччині — спокійна вода й легкий берег. Каньйон починається з 15 м і йде до 30.

Для першої поїздки за кордон із клубом — ідеальне місце.

posts.title: Абу-Рамада: коралові сади
posts.text:
Риф біля Хургади, мілко й барвисто. Риби-наполеони підпливають майже впритул.

Гарне місце, щоб показати новачкам Червоне море.

submissions.name: Blue Lakes Quarry
submissions.description: A flooded sand quarry north of Kyiv. Clear water in spring, a sunken bus at 12 m used for training. Entry from the beach on the east side.

divers.name: Sofia Alvarez
divers.bio: Marine biologist from Mérida. Cenotes, sharks and long boat trips.

dives.notes: Stalactites at 40 m, Caribbean reef sharks.
Hammerhead wall. Whale shark at the end.
Silvertips and a manta on every dive.

reviews.text: Hold on to the rocks and watch the hammerheads pass. Only for experienced divers: strong surge and currents.
Famous, and the stalactites are impressive, but the dive itself is short and deep. The walls of Half Moon Caye are more fun.
Crystal-clear fresh water and incredible light. Cavern only: stay within sight of the exit.
Easy drift along coral towers. Lots of turtles.

warnings.text: A diver was swept off the site in a down-current last week and surfaced 1 km away. Carry an SMB and a whistle, and stay close to your guide.

posts.title: Galápagos liveaboard diary
posts.text: Eight days, twenty dives and more hammerheads than I can count. Darwin and Wolf deserve their reputation, but the currents are serious: every dive started with a negative entry and ended with a long drift.

posts.title: Dos Ojos: light in the cenote
posts.text:
The first cavern of Dos Ojos is lit by two sinkholes. Halocline at 9 metres makes the water shimmer like glass.

Stay on the line and respect the cave signs. The cavern zone is enough for an unforgettable dive.

posts.title: Palancar Reef drift
posts.text:
Cozumel's current carries you along coral towers taller than a house. Just relax and steer with your fins.

We saw two turtles and a nurse shark under a ledge.

posts.title: Gordon Rocks, the washing machine
posts.text:
Strong surge and a three-way current, but hammerheads in the channel. Stay low and hold the rocks when you need to.

Not for a first Galapagos dive. Do a checkout dive before.

posts.title: Mantas at Roca Partida
posts.text:
Five days of crossing to reach the Socorro islands, and it was worth every hour. Giant mantas came back again and again.

They seem to enjoy the bubbles. Stay still and let them choose the distance.

submissions.name: Cenote Angelita
submissions.description: A cenote with a hydrogen sulphide cloud at 30 m that looks like an underwater river.
submissions.reason: The coordinates point to the jungle 3 km from the cenote. Please resubmit with the entrance location and add the depth of the cloud to the description.

divers.name: James Whitaker
divers.bio: Weekend diver from Brisbane. Reef, wrecks and night dives.

certificates.reason: The card photo was missing and the issuing school could not be identified. Please add a photo of the card.

dives.notes: Potato cods as big as me.

reviews.text: Sit on the sand, point your torch up and wait. One of the best dives of my life, and it is only 12 m deep.
Friendly potato cods, easy conditions. A must on any Ribbon Reefs trip.
Remote, vertical walls and sharks. Only by liveaboard.
Big wreck with currents on top. Penetration only with a guide.

posts.title: Cod Hole, potato cod and friends
posts.text:
The cod at Cod Hole are not shy at all. One followed me for the whole dive like a puppy.

The reef top is at 15 metres, which makes it an easy dive with lots of light.

posts.title: Osprey Reef wall
posts.text:
The wall drops to a thousand metres. We hung at 25 metres and watched grey reef sharks patrol.

The visibility was over 40 metres. Hard to beat anywhere.

posts.title: Navy Pier is a must
posts.text:
Exmouth's Navy Pier has more life per square metre than any place I know. Nudibranchs, frogfish and a wobbegong.

You need to book through the one licensed operator, so plan ahead.

posts.title: Spiegel Grove for wreck fans
posts.text:
A 155-metre ship sitting upright at 40 metres off Key Largo. The deck is at 20 metres.

The current can be strong. Use the mooring line down and up.

posts.title: Manta night dive in Kona
posts.text:
Lights on the bottom attract plankton, and the plankton attract mantas. They loop around inches from your head.

Kneel, keep your hands in and enjoy the show.

divers.name: Ingrid Larsen
divers.bio: Cold-water diver from Bergen. Drysuit all year round.

reviews.text: Clearest water you will ever see. You need a drysuit certification, and the 2-degree water is no joke for your hands.
Open-ocean seamount, two hours by boat. Mobulas in summer.

warnings.text: The park now requires a dry suit certificate and 10 logged dry suit dives. Bring your log, the operators check it.

posts.title: Silfra between two continents
posts.text:
Two degrees and a hundred metres of visibility. You can touch America and Europe at the same time.

Drysuit and dry gloves are a must. My hands still remember.

posts.title: Princess Alice Bank and the mobulas
posts.text:
Two hours by boat from Pico, in the middle of the Atlantic. Mobulas came in a group of twenty.

The water was blue and 21 degrees. Very different from home.

posts.title: El Bajón in winter
posts.text:
El Hierro's El Bajón is a volcanic pinnacle full of life. Barracuda schools circle the top.

The water is 18 degrees in winter, so a drysuit is welcome.

posts.title: Gozo Blue Hole with a drysuit
posts.text:
Everyone else was in a wetsuit, but my drysuit kept me warm for an hour. The arch at 15 metres is the best part.

Watch out for waves at the entry on windy days.

posts.title: Cold water, warm heart
posts.text:
People ask why I dive in four degrees. The answer: kelp, visibility and quiet.

Good thermal protection is everything. Layer up and you will love it.

divers.name: Nomvula Dlamini
divers.bio: Shark diver from Durban. Aliwal Shoal is my home reef.

reviews.text: Ragged-tooth sharks from June to November. Surf launch from the beach is part of the adventure.
Best night dive in the Maldives: whitetip reef sharks hunting all around you.
Strong currents on the plateaus, but the sharks are worth it. Dive it from a liveaboard to beat the day boats.

warnings.text: Ragged-tooth sharks are resting in the Cathedral (June to November). Do not block the entrance and keep 3 m away.

posts.title: Aliwal Shoal Cathedral and the raggies
posts.text:
From July to November, ragged-tooth sharks gather in the Cathedral. They hover still, teeth out, but calm.

Keep your distance and do not block the entrance.

posts.title: Two Mile Reef in Sodwana
posts.text:
Easy, shallow and full of colour. A perfect reef for new divers.

We saw a potato bass and a turtle sleeping under a ledge.

posts.title: Night sharks at Maaya Thila
posts.text:
Maaya Thila at night means white-tip sharks hunting in the torchlight. It is fast and exciting.

Stay with your buddy and keep the torch away from their eyes.

posts.title: Banana Reef, the Maldives classic
posts.text:
One of the oldest dive sites in the Maldives, and still beautiful. Caves, overhangs and a lot of fish.

Current depends on the tide, so ask the guide.

posts.title: Why I love shark diving
posts.text:
Sharks are not monsters. They are careful, curious and important for the reef.

Every shark dive I do, I try to show people that.
